Columns and images stay Quarto's layout. Askr restyles grouped tabsets.

## Columns

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
The left column is half of the content measure.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
The right column is the other half. A narrow screen stacks them.
:::
:::

## Tabset

These two groups stay in step. Choosing Palace or AEDT in one group selects it in the other. The article underneath does not sit in a second card.

::: {.panel-tabset group="backend"}
## Palace

Palace uses the shared layout and its own electrostatic input.

## AEDT

AEDT Q3D uses the same layout and its own input binding.
:::

::: {.panel-tabset group="backend"}
## Palace

The eigenmode result is read from the Palace run.

## AEDT

The eigenmode result is read from the HFSS run.
:::

## Image

Images in this document come from Embla. The chart below is
its bars-and-markers figure, saved here as a static image. Quarto's folded
cell keeps the embed source behind Source and shows the image underneath.

{{< include ../_includes/_figures-image-cell.qmd >}}

A page that only needs the picture, without a source disclosure, embeds it
directly:

```markdown
![Bars with semantic markers](images/bars-semantic-markers.png)
```

## Image viewer

Click an independent figure or its button to open Askr's floating viewer.
Use + / −, Fit, drag to pan or pinch to zoom. Escape returns to the article.

## Theme toggle

Quarto keeps two outputs from one cell and shows one of them. `body.quarto-dark` hides `.light-content`; `body.quarto-light` hides `.dark-content`. Askr's dark stylesheet is marked `data-mode="dark"`, so the header toggle adds and removes `quarto-dark` with the stylesheet.

Emit the light output first, then the dark output:

{{< include ../_includes/_figures-theme-toggle-cell.qmd >}}

The same order works for a Plotly figure: draw the light figure, then the dark figure, under `#| renderings: [light, dark]`. The figure colors are baked into each output. The toggle does not recolor a single picture.

## Diagram

This simple, unwrapped Mermaid block stays native in the article and does not
add viewer controls:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  Areas[Areas] --> Pages[Page List]
  Pages --> Article[Article]
  Article --> Sections[Section List]
```

This gallery does not ship a photograph.

## Mermaid viewer {#mermaid-viewer}

Wrap exactly one native Mermaid block in `.askr-mermaid-view` to add a
`View diagram` button below the rendered graph. The graph remains in the
article; the button opens its floating viewer. The wide flow below keeps its
natural width in a keyboard-focusable horizontal scroll region.

::: {.askr-wide-figure aria-label="Public documentation flow"}
::: {.askr-mermaid-view view-label="View diagram"}
```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph author["Authoring"]
    direction TB
    source["Write one native<br/>Mermaid block"] --> wrapper["Add the optional<br/>viewer wrapper"]
  end
  subgraph build["Build and publish"]
    direction TB
    render["Quarto renders<br/>the HTML page"] --> publish["Publish the<br/>documentation"]
  end
  subgraph reader["Reading"]
    direction TB
    article["Diagram appears<br/>in the article"] --> open["Choose View diagram"] --> inspect["Zoom, pan or Fit<br/>in the floating viewer"] --> close["Close and return<br/>to the article"]
  end
  wrapper --> render
  publish --> article
```
:::
:::

Use `View diagram` to open the rendered graph in the floating viewer. The
adjacent `Mermaid source` disclosure below the graph expands the authored block
on demand; its `Copy` button copies the source. See the
[Mermaid viewer guide](../usage/image-viewer.qmd#mermaid-viewer) for controls
and limits.

## Limits

The columns, tabset and simple diagram fit the article width. The wider flow
uses `.askr-wide-figure` to keep its natural size and scroll horizontally. A
floating viewer can zoom, but does not replace readable labels or logical
grouping. Redraw a diagram if its labels or relationships remain hard to
follow; do not shrink its text to force a poster into a column.
